openings.claim: Refine the incumbent into an explicitly ordered release-seat-clamp joint and compare its seating procedure against visually tight clamping.
openings.delta: Keep the incumbent's two plywood datum-and-stop pockets, movable plates and captive threaded hardware. Change the positioning dependency: release each plate enough to seat the rod against both datum faces and its insertion stop before tightening. Clamp travel handles the 18 mm replacement without moving fixed references. Cord retains release-prone parts; no drilling, adhesive or permanent marking touches rods. All assembly and adjustment remain hand operated inside the 90 mm cube.
openings.prediction: The nearest rival is visual tightness: close the same plates when the rod looks secure, without deliberate datum seating. Ordered seating predicts fewer returns outside the 2 mm circle, including after diameter substitution, while retaining ten-second 10 N load stability. Similar errors under both procedures, or ordered seating's load displacement, defeats the claimed advantage. Plywood flex and inconsistent clamp force remain alternative explanations; no result is supplied.
openings.probe: Fabricate and check the incumbent within 100 minutes: envelope, hand removal of either rod, clamp travel and retention of every component. If these fail, stop. Use two procedural configurations on the same hardware, each with five exchanges per rod position and four ten-second load trials. Substitute 18 mm for the last two exchanges of the 19 mm position. Log target-circle return, loaded position, exchange time and whether deliberate seating was completed. Every successful exchange must take less than forty seconds. Allocate the twenty-minute test period before starting; if measurement and procedure-switch time cannot fit, report incomplete testing. Compare procedure-specific failures without claiming statistical proof or deploying an unverified joint.
assumptions: The incumbent pocket connections, stops and plates can share eight bolts without interference; geometry is unverified.
Six plywood pieces and available cord suffice for stiffness and captive release.
Hand clamping, datum accuracy and remaining test time may be insufficient.

assessment: One conditional engineering explanation becomes a comparative probe. Hard constraints remain intact, but fabrication feasibility and repeatability remain uncertain.

lineage.reason: Preserves the joint concept while adding a controlled seating-procedure rival and explicit comparative defeat conditions.
